title: Remnants
text: A state of alert was declared… and three days have now passed. We’ve been unable to track down the group claiming to represent the Melromarc Army; the only evidence so far has been reports of sightings outside the country. I remember Father muttering as he gazed up at the sky, “I just hope a war doesn’t break out.”

And so, a state of high tension persisted within Siltvelt. During that time, Siltvelt informed Faubrey—based on my explanation—that the Whip Hero’s gang had been keeping a monster that was posing as the Claw Hero… and that they had attempted to kill us in retaliation for that monster’s death.
However… the situation took an even worse turn. At noon on the third day, a messenger rushed in, flinging open the doors to the Throne Room.
“The Shieldfreeden Army has declared war on our Siltvelt!”
“The Shieldfreeden Army is attacking while we haven’t even figured out the Melromarc invasion yet!?”
“Yes! Shieldfreeden’s representative, Nelshen, declared before the nation that they had treacherously lured and killed the ‘Whip Hero,’ who had tried to challenge the waves out of goodwill!”

With that, the messenger showed us the video crystal. On the screen, a battered blue pig is oinking away. Sensing that I couldn’t make out what was being said, my Father stood beside me and explained it to me.

“‘We, the well-meaning… Takt, the Whip Hero who wished for world peace, and our divine Dragon Lord, fell into a treacherous trap set by the Shield Heroes and Spear Heroes and met a tragic end. That’s right—they killed their own country’s Hero of the Claws, and to top it off, they even eliminated Lord Takt, the Hero of the Whip… Such… inhumane acts simply cannot be tolerated! Justice is on our side—we are justice! We must not allow such evildoers to run rampant in this world! Destroy Siltvelt, which defends evil! Vengeance is ours!”… “Enough is enough!”
My Father snaps, looking thoroughly disgusted. I, too, am at the end of my rope. I still regret that we couldn’t wipe them all out back then.

“They launched a preemptive attack themselves, yet now that they’ve been defeated, they’re making up this excuse to start a war? On top of that, they’ve gone and declared that we killed the Hero of the Claws—even though they were the ones who actually killed him!”
“They’ve announced it to the entire world. Our nation will refute it, but I can’t imagine that vile country would give up the just cause it needs to invade us…”
“No way… Was this all part of the Wise King’s strategy?!”
The leader of the Shusaku clan blurts out in shock. A heavy silence settles over the room as the leading figures of Siltvelt gather in the throne room.

“An invasion by a joint force of the Melromarc and Shieldfreeden armies…? But doesn’t that assume Takt’s surprise attack will fail? I can’t imagine such a reckless strategy would be allowed to succeed.”

“It is said that the Wise King is the one who turns the impossible into reality. Just think of how much our nation, Siltvelt, has suffered in the past… I never imagined the Three Heroes Church would make the unthinkable a reality—joining forces with Shieldfreeden…”
“I see… I thought I might be overthinking it, but…”
“The Shieldfreeden Army has seized the aircraft that the Whip Hero had been developing on his own, and they’re invading our country at breakneck speed!”
“The only thing you can do with an airplane… is bomb, right?”

At Father’s words, the senior officials’ faces turned pale. Well, as it turned out, the airplanes didn’t make it all the way to Siltvelt Castle, but reports came in that towns near Shieldfreeden had been bombed, causing massive damage.
“Furthermore, remnants of the Whip Hero’s gang are carrying out terrorist acts in various locations throughout our country!”
“The damage is catastrophic… This has nothing to do with the Shield Hero anymore!”
My Father leaned forward and declared this. At that, the dignitaries saluted and began to pray.
“Shield Hero, please quell your wrath… We will certainly overcome this battle with our own strength.”
“I was the one who said that in the first place, but this is going too far…”

That’s right—Father had previously asked them not to wage war in his name. The people of Siltvelt are trying to honor that promise. What a noble sentiment. Father seems eager to help them, so let’s come up with a plan.
“Father, how about we try this?”
“What?”
“Takt’s remnants are part of the Hero’s gang… this is an act of aggression instigated by the Hero. And their goal is revenge against me for killing Takt.”
“…You’re right. Since Takt’s remnants are the Hero’s problem, Motoyasu and I will go around defeating them, so everyone else should fight against Shieldfreeden and the Melromarc Army!”
“We are grateful for the self-sacrifice of the Spear Hero and the mercy of the Shield Hero.”
“For now, let’s do whatever we can to minimize the casualties among our citizens!”
And so, my Father and I set out to eliminate Takt’s remnants. My spear is aching to kill a pig. And my heart desires it as well.
“Aiming Lancer X!”
“Ooohhh—”

Just by walking through the town—which looks peaceful at first glance—while pretending to be spacey and full of openings, the remnants of Takt start gathering around us. It’s surprisingly easy. They’re so simple-minded—it’s almost anticlimactic.
“Did they seriously think they could beat Motoyasu-kun just because their level was higher…?”
“Well, pigs are generally incompetent, after all.”
“Is that really how it is?”
Pigs sniping with rifles from afar, pigs slashing at me with swords up close, pigs firing Magic. I took down every single one of those pigs.
“Next, I’m scheduled to give a speech about the truth in the western part of the country.”
“So that means more pigs are coming, huh?”
“Yeah, I guess so. Seriously… I wonder how many of them are gathering.”
“Nothing but pigs, huh?”
With Yuki-chan and the others by my side, along with my Father, I’ll move forward with our next plan.

“That’s right. What a harem. Women really are scary, aren’t they? Well… I suppose this is just their way of showing affection, but I wish they’d put themselves in the shoes of the ones being led around by the nose.”
“They’re ignoring the despicable deeds they’ve committed themselves and instead are calling for revenge, aren’t they?”

“It’s not like I can’t understand how they feel…　But that’s a different matter altogether. According to Motoyasu-kun, he’s the very one who killed numerous Heroes in the future, isn’t he? To witness that and still approve of it—that’s a grave sin in this world.”

Heroes bear the responsibility of saving the world from the Waves. Hiding the fact that he was killing those Heroes amounts to an act of treason against the world and a barbaric act that increases the number of victims. To turn a blind eye to criminal acts and blindly trust the one you love—that’s just like a pig, isn’t it? It makes me want to vomit.

“Well… thanks to our efforts, it seems the number of remnants hiding out in Siltvelt has decreased somewhat, but it’s kind of short-sighted—or rather, it seems we’ve only managed to wipe out the combat-oriented remnants.”
“Next up is dealing with those devious pigs who rely on cunning.”

“That’s how it’ll go. Most of them seem to have fled to Shieldfreeden, which advocates for war, so it’ll be tricky. A diversion… It seems there are also remnants carrying out terrorist acts within Siltvelt, so I imagine my future self had a hard time with that, didn’t he?”
“I have no such memory.”
“Huh? Even though there are so many remnants running rampant like this?”

My father asks me with a puzzled look. Now, how exactly did my future father deal with those Takt pigs? I, Motoyasu, am rather unfamiliar with the official duties my father used to handle. Still… I do recall that those Takt pigs were executed.
“In the future, did you capture Takt alive, strip him of his Seven Star Weapons using the power of the Holy Weapons… and then carry out a public execution?”
“…A public execution?”

My father is looking at me with an expression that seems to say, “Did my future father do something again?” I, Motoyasu, will continue to recount the exploits of my future father for all eternity. Um… let’s see… I believe…
“Right… I recall that all the remnants were executed right in front of Takt.”
“Executed right in front of him… Did I take the lead on that?”
“I didn’t ask about that. Even you, Father, looked thoroughly fed up once the executions were over.”
“Did you get tired of watching Takt’s remnants get executed? Or was it because you were forced to witness that method of execution? Which is it?”
“I don’t know.”
I don’t know either. But I do remember that you looked a bit worn out back then.
“Publicly executing those women right in front of Takt… that’s a terribly cruel method…”
Father muttered with a look of disgust. That’s true. But sometimes, that very cruelty is what wins people over. Making them think, ‘I don’t want to be their enemy,’ is a formidable power in itself.

“If I recall correctly… the executioner did state Takt’s charges. ‘The crime of treating the world as one’s personal property is grave. Tact and his party, who posed as heroes, shall be given a punishment more agonizing than death.” I believe that’s what it was.”
“…I can’t say I don’t understand that sentiment. Anyway, getting back to the topic—don’t you remember, Motoyasu, how he gathered those stragglers?”
“When we defeated Takt directly, I’d been asked to take on the Wave faction, so I didn’t witness it firsthand.”
“I see… It would’ve been easier if you’d remembered, even if it was just secondhand.”
Hmm… Let me try to dig through my memories. I seem to recall Midori telling me something about that. Let’s see…
“That’s right! I think the pigs surrounding Takt were captured alive, while the ones in other countries were gathered through information manipulation.”
That’s right—I just remembered Midori telling me she’d heard that from her Father.
